solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Excellent meal, but requiring no repetition (5)

indicatorNotes.requiring no repetition: the meal's name has a letter said twice in a row, and a thing that needs no repeating keeps only one of them

blocks.note: one of the two Ps goes

annotation.surface: A diner praises a meal but asks not to be served the same thing twice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Excellent meal' reads as one phrase, but the split comes straight after 'Excellent'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: super is informal British praise, as in 'a super idea'.

entries.clue: Party in charge in Asian country after uprising (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the charge abbreviation is placed in the middle of the country's name
indicatorNotes.uprising: an uprising goes upward, and in a down clue going up means reading the letters bottom to top

annotation.surface: A political party takes power in an Asian country after a revolt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political, and 'uprising' backs that up; but the party is a get-together and the uprising flips the country with its new passenger inside, so the charge letters read backwards too.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a social is an informal gathering, like a church or club social evening.

entries.clue: Request certain suggestions about river journeys offering a good time (8,5)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in 'round about': the suggestions are placed around the river letter

annotation.surface: Someone asks for firm ideas about which river cruises will be fun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River journeys' looks like one phrase, but 'river' belongs to the wordplay and the definition starts at 'journeys'.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase: pleasure trips are outings taken purely for enjoyment rather than business.

entries.clue: Profligate vacation’s ending in French city (5)

indicatorNotes.ending: a word's ending is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a roué is a dissolute man, a rake

annotation.surface: A spendthrift finishes his holiday in a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Profligate' is an adjective in the surface but has to be read as a noun, the rake himself.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Rouen is the historic capital of Normandy, on the Seine.

entries.clue: Money received of those people, having acquired a promenade? (4,3,3)

indicatorNotes.having acquired: to acquire something is to take it in, so the pronoun takes the A inside itself

blocks.note: the take is the money taken in, as at a box office
the article, used as a letter

annotation.surface: Someone asks what a group earned after they got hold of a seafront promenade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A promenade' looks like a noun phrase, but the A is swallowed by THEIR and 'promenade' is a verb, to stroll.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb sense: to promenade is to stroll for pleasure and fresh air, the old idiom's meaning.

entries.clue: Rocker’s equivalent to this roller? (7)

blocks.note: the word that can replace 'rocker' in 'off one's rocker', meaning mad
a wheeled cart for shopping or luggage

annotation.surface: A question comparing something that rocks with something that rolls.
annotation.walkthrough: The link is an idiom: someone crazy is 'off their rocker', or equally 'off' the answer, so in that phrase the two words swap freely.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an idiom partner for rocker in phrases meaning mad, and a wheeled cart that rolls.

entries.clue: Delivery chap who’s peckish? (9,3)

blocks.note: reads as a courier or postman; he delivers greetings in person
reads as hungry; really, given to pecks, little kisses

annotation.surface: A delivery man who is feeling hungry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peckish' normally means a bit hungry; here it means given to pecks, the little kisses this messenger delivers.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: a kissogram is a greeting delivered in person with a kiss, so its courier deals in pecks.

entries.clue: It’s provocative carrying stone clubs, for example (4,4)

indicatorNotes.carrying: to carry something is to hold it, so the provocative word holds the stone and clubs letters inside

blocks.note: a tease is someone or something provocative

annotation.surface: Something provocative is carried by stone-age clubs, as an illustration.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stone clubs' suggests cavemen, but it is two abbreviations; a stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a test case is an example whose outcome sets the pattern for others.

entries.clue: Prepare Parisian who will cut recording (5)

indicatorNotes.will cut: to cut something is to slice into it, so the French word lands in the middle of the record

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: Get ready the Parisian who will edit a recording.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' is the usual signal to translate the next word into French.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to equip someone is to fit them out, getting them ready.

entries.clue: To sum up about computers etc, lately disheartened to a great extent (10)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in 'around': the summing-up phrase goes around the computers abbreviation
indicatorNotes.disheartened: the heart of a word is its middle, so a disheartened word keeps only its ends

blocks.note: in fine is a formal phrase meaning finally, in summary
the first and last letters of lately

annotation.surface: A summary of how computers have lately become far more dispiriting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In fine' is an old Latin-derived phrase for 'in short', rare outside crosswords and legal prose.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase of degree: infinitely, used loosely, means immensely, as in 'infinitely better'.

entries.clue: Learned person positioned to accept leading figures (6)

indicatorNotes.to accept: to accept something is to take it in, so the seated word takes the front-runners inside

blocks.note: the van is the vanguard, the people at the front

annotation.surface: A scholar is placed to receive the most important people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading figures' looks like VIPs; here it is the van, the front of an army or movement.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: savant is French for a learned person, a scholar of deep knowledge.

entries.clue: American President initially has reduced chilly reception, being unable to make speech? (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the opening letters of American President count
indicatorNotes.reduced: a reduced word has been cut down, here losing its final letter

blocks.note: a chilly reception is ice, cut short

annotation.surface: An American president given a frosty welcome is lost for words.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a president too offended to speak; the question mark marks the definition as a playful paraphrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical term: aphasia is loss of the power to produce or understand language, often after a stroke.

entries.clue: A passion arising in celebrity circus performer (9)

indicatorNotes.arising: something arising goes up, and in a down clue going up means reading bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the upturned piece is placed inside the celebrity word

blocks.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

annotation.surface: A craze rising among the famous for a circus act.
annotation.walkthrough: The insertion point is just after the first letter of the celebrity word, which is easy to miss because both pieces begin with A.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: an aerialist performs high in the air, on trapeze or tightrope.

entries.clue: Impressive tango? Rash going topless (5)

indicatorNotes.going topless: losing one's top; in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Tango is T in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone praises a daring tango, or warns against rashly stripping off.
annotation.walkthrough: Tasty for impressive is British slang, as in a tasty goal or a tasty line-up.
annotation.definitionFit: A British slang sense: tasty describes something formidable or admirable, like a tasty line-up.

entries.clue: Comedy film that’ll have you thinking of better activities? (1,3,2,3,5)

annotation.definition: Comedy film that’ll have you thinking of better activities?

blocks.note: a straight description: the title of a film comedy

blocks.clueFragment: that’ll have you thinking of better activities?
blocks.note: reads as preferring other pastimes; really, the activities of a better, one who bets

annotation.surface: A film so dull it makes you wish you were doing something else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as more pleasant; it is one who bets, so the activities are wagers on horses.
annotation.definitionFit: A title with a pun: the 1937 Marx Brothers comedy is set around a racetrack full of gamblers.

entries.clue: Ready to accept unimaginative cut in revised course (9)

indicatorNotes.cut: a cut word has been trimmed, here losing its final letter
indicatorNotes.in: the trimmed word is placed inside the rearranged one
indicatorNotes.revised: a revised text has been reworked, so its letters are reordered

annotation.surface: A college is ready to accept cuts to a course that was too dull.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the thing being accepted; it only shortens the unimaginative word.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: credulous people are too ready to accept what they are told, lacking scepticism.

entries.clue: Duffers upset with this society after time, old fogeys (7,6)

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a new order

annotation.surface: Incompetents annoyed with a club after a while: stuffy old men.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like an order instruction, but everything is mixed together, so it only adds the time letter to the pile.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a stuffed shirt is a pompous, old-fashioned person, much like a fogey.

entries.clue: Club second to enter sports venue beside lake (7)

indicatorNotes.to enter: to enter a place is to go inside it, so the second goes inside the venue
indicatorNotes.beside: beside means next to, so the lake letter is added on after

blocks.note: an arena is a sports venue

annotation.surface: A club enters its second team into a stadium by a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: The London football club fits the sports picture, which is why 'Club' does not feel like a definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Arsenal is a Premier League football club in north London.

entries.clue: Love cricket club to capture trophy, an ultimately quality possession (9)

indicatorNotes.to capture: to capture something is to hold it prisoner, so the two letters of the club enclose the trophy and 'an'
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter counts

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, O

annotation.surface: A cricket club loves winning a trophy, which is a prized possession.
annotation.walkthrough: Both 'trophy' and 'an' go inside the club abbreviation, splitting its two Cs.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: occupancy is the holding and use of a property, a form of possession.

entries.clue: Precipitous cliff alongside right-hand edge of railway — alarming (5)

indicatorNotes.alongside: alongside means next to, so the two parts sit side by side
indicatorNotes.right-hand edge of: we read left to right, so a word's right-hand edge is its last letter

blocks.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

annotation.surface: A railway line runs along the edge of a sheer cliff, which is frightening.
annotation.walkthrough: Scar for a cliff is a northern English word, common in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scary is informal for frightening, causing alarm.

entries.clue: Important measures having impact, limiting female work at night (9,5)

indicatorNotes.limiting: to limit something is to hem it in, so the impact word hems in the female letter

annotation.surface: Serious steps that restrict women working at night.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like employment law, with 'female work at night' as one phrase; 'female' is only an F.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the graveyard shift is the overnight stint, named for the dead quiet of the small hours.

entries.clue: Old film star’s answer provided while tucking into Orvieto? (9)

indicatorNotes.while tucking into: to tuck into food or drink is to get stuck in, so the pieces go inside the wine

blocks.note: Orvieto is an Italian white wine, so an example of vino

annotation.surface: A silent-era star answers a question while enjoying Italian wine.
annotation.walkthrough: Orvieto is a white wine from Umbria, and the question mark says it stands for wine in general.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Rudolph Valentino was the great romantic idol of 1920s silent films.

entries.clue: Not to be swallowed, even after removing first couple of crusts (8)

indicatorNotes.after removing: removing means taking out, so the named letters leave the word

blocks.note: hard to swallow means hard to believe
C and R, the first two letters of crusts, are taken out

annotation.surface: Even crusts trimmed at the edges are not fit to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'Not to be swallowed' twice on purpose: a story you cannot swallow is unbelievable, and food you cannot swallow is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The literal sense: food that is not to be swallowed is unfit to eat.

entries.clue: Diplomacy is hedging about means to achieve end (7)

indicatorNotes.hedging: a hedge encloses a field, so the short word encloses the 'about' letter

annotation.surface: Diplomacy is a matter of evasion in pursuit of a goal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hedging' looks like the diplomat's evasiveness; it is a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: tactics are the planned moves used to reach a particular goal.

entries.clue: Very absorbed by period leading to spring (10)

indicatorNotes.leading to: one thing leading to another comes before it, so the period goes first

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time
a bound is a leap or spring

annotation.surface: Someone is utterly engrossed in a season that leads into spring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a leap.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: someone spellbound is held as if by magic, completely engrossed.

entries.clue: Two were annoying about Frenchmen having moved in (10)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in 'around': the numeral goes around the Frenchmen

blocks.note: MM = Messieurs, the French plural of Mr

annotation.surface: A pair of locals complained that some Frenchmen had moved in nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two' is the Roman numeral II, split so the Frenchmen can sit between its strokes.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: to immigrate is to come into a new country to settle.

entries.clue: Daring problem linked to uranium, say, on the radio (10)

indicatorNotes.linked to: linked means joined, so the two sounds are run together
indicatorNotes.on the radio: radio carries only sound, so what counts is how the words are said, not spelt

blocks.note: uranium is an example of a metal
a sum is an arithmetic problem

annotation.surface: A bold radio item about a problem with uranium.
annotation.walkthrough: The uranium sound comes first in the answer though 'problem' is first in the clue, because 'linked to' allows either order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mettlesome means full of mettle, spirited and brave.

entries.clue: Lots of strands and upturned components in feature of dress (9,5)

indicatorNotes.upturned: turned upside down; in a down clue that means reading the word bottom to top

blocks.note: spaghetti is a mass of long pasta strands

annotation.surface: Many threads and upside-down pieces go into a dress design.
annotation.walkthrough: The dress picture makes 'strands' sound like thread; they are strands of pasta.
annotation.definitionFit: A fashion term: a spaghetti strap is a thin shoulder strap on a dress or top.

entries.clue: Where doctors work — distribute The Lancet here? Mostly (6,6)

indicatorNotes.distribute: to distribute is to hand things out in all directions, so the letters are scattered
indicatorNotes.Mostly: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder; The Lancet is a medical journal

annotation.surface: A clinic plans to hand out copies of The Lancet.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lancet is a leading British medical journal, which is why the surface feels like a doctors' waiting room.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term: a health centre is a local building housing GP surgeries and nurses.

entries.clue: Excuse an ex-tutee freaking out (9)

indicatorNotes.freaking out: someone freaking out loses control, so the letters run wild into a new order

annotation.surface: A former pupil loses control and a teacher looks for an excuse.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'ex-tutee' is ignored; the fodder is just the nine letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to extenuate is to lessen the seriousness of an offence, partly excusing it.

entries.clue: Outcome of trial? Exiled to that place in parts of London (8)

indicatorNotes.in parts of London: in Cockney parts of London the H is dropped from the start of words

blocks.note: HENCE, away from here, said with its H dropped

annotation.surface: The verdict: banishment to a certain district of London.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockney, the speech of London's East End, drops initial H, so HENCE is said 'ENCE.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: the sentence is the punishment handed down at the end of a criminal trial.

entries.clue: One Greek character attached to … a burning wheel, apparently (5)

annotation.definition: One Greek character attached to … a burning wheel, apparently

blocks.note: xi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the rest of the &lit reading, adding no letters

annotation.surface: A figure of Greek myth, strapped to a flaming wheel.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: Ixion was a Greek character bound to a burning wheel; the ellipsis marks the join.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue tells the myth: Zeus punished Ixion by binding him to a fiery wheel forever.

entries.clue: Speculative account taking in broadcast media (8)

indicatorNotes.taking in: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the account holds the scattered letters
indicatorNotes.broadcast: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are scattered into a new order

annotation.surface: A theoretical report about the broadcast media.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast media' looks like television and radio; 'broadcast' is scattering the letters of MEDIA.
annotation.definitionFit: A secondary sense: an academic question is theoretical, of no practical consequence.

entries.clue: Formalities favouring Conservative in contrivance (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the party letter is placed in the middle of the device word

blocks.note: a tool is a device, a contrivance

annotation.surface: Official procedures that favour the Conservatives in some scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contrivance' suggests a political plot; it is simply a device.
annotation.definitionFit: A plural paraphrase: protocol is the system of formal etiquette for official occasions.

entries.clue: Encouraging to receive a great success in old sport (13)

indicatorNotes.to receive: to receive something is to take it in, so the encouraging word takes the success inside

blocks.note: a riot is a huge hit, as in 'the show was a riot'

annotation.surface: Spectators cheer a triumph in an ancient sport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great success' as RIOT is informal, from a comedy that is 'a riot'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: chariot driving was a racing sport of ancient Greece and Rome.

entries.clue: Expensive rental to secure church? There are obstacles to participating in this (12)

annotation.definition: There are obstacles to participating in this

indicatorNotes.to secure: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the rental holds the church letters inside

blocks.note: a lease is a rental agreement

annotation.surface: A pricey lease on a church faces barriers to joining in.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like red tape about taking part; the obstacles are literal fences and water jumps.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: runners in this race must clear hurdles and water jumps along the way.

entries.clue: Italian composer lost his grip around finale of piece (8)

indicatorNotes.lost: something lost has gone astray, so the letters stray into a new order
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around the final letter of piece

annotation.surface: A composer loses control near the end of a performance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lost his grip' reads as one idiom about the composer; 'lost' is the signal to rearrange the two words after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Ottorino Respighi wrote The Pines of Rome and The Fountains of Rome.

entries.clue: Difficult situation, nothing less, accepted by Athenian soccer team? (8)

indicatorNotes.less: less means minus, so the zero letter is taken away
indicatorNotes.accepted by: to be accepted is to be let in, so the shortened word goes inside the Athenian word

blocks.note: a hole is a fix, a tight spot
O, the zero, is what is removed

annotation.surface: An Athenian football club is in a tight spot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing less' looks like 'no less than'; it tells you to remove the O.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Athletic is part of many club names, such as Charlton Athletic or Athletic Bilbao.

entries.clue: No good taking on excellent old New Zealand tree (5)

indicatorNotes.taking on: to take on is to add to oneself, so the other pieces are attached after

blocks.note: A1 = first class, with the 1 read as I

annotation.surface: A useless old tree is saved by adding something first-rate.
annotation.walkthrough: A1, first class, is written AI in crosswords because the digit looks like the letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the ngaio is a small evergreen coastal tree native to New Zealand.

entries.clue: Surface on a sea yielding zero for lobster or similar (10)

indicatorNotes.yielding: to yield is to give up, so the sea word gives up its zero

blocks.note: a crust is a hard surface layer
places the next piece after the crust
O, which the ocean gives up

annotation.surface: A lobster surfaces on the open sea.
annotation.walkthrough: The sea setting suits a lobster, but 'Surface' is a noun here, a hard outer layer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lobsters, crabs and shrimps all belong to the crustaceans.

entries.clue: Examine Bill, initially lacking a certain hormone (12)

indicatorNotes.initially lacking: missing at the start, so the bill word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a bill is a printed poster
one = a certain, as in 'one Mr Smith'

annotation.surface: A doctor checks a patient called Bill and finds him short of a hormone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a printed notice, as in 'stick no bills'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: testosterone is the chief male sex hormone.

entries.clue: Majestic display fed by complete source of electricity (9)

indicatorNotes.fed by: something fed has food put inside it, so the display takes in the other pieces
indicatorNotes.source of: a source is where something starts, so only the first letter counts

annotation.surface: A grand illuminated display is powered by a full electricity supply.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints a lit-up sign; the power source is only the letter E.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: sovereign describes supreme royal authority, hence regal and majestic.

entries.clue: USA misrepresented by one in individual novel (10)

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order
indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters and the one are placed inside the individual

annotation.surface: An American portrayed falsely by a single figure in a work of fiction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' could be an adjective meaning new; here it is a book.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Persuasion is Jane Austen's last completed novel, published in 1817.

entries.clue: Tyrant upheld nonsense to support suppressing court (8)

indicatorNotes.upheld: held up; in a down clue, lifting a word means reading it bottom to top
indicatorNotes.suppressing: to suppress is to hold down, so the upturned letters hold the court inside them

annotation.surface: A despot backed by nonsense props up his regime by crushing the courts.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversal happens first and the insertion second, so the court abbreviation reads forwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a dictator rules with absolute power, as a tyrant does.

entries.clue: Another artist included in most of Michelangelo’s work (2,5)

indicatorNotes.in: the abbreviation is placed inside the shortened statue
indicatorNotes.most of: most but not all, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A rival painter slipped into most of Michelangelo's output.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' links back to Michelangelo: the definition is a second Renaissance artist.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Leonardo da Vinci was Michelangelo's great contemporary and rival.

entries.clue: A lot of fresh confusion after invasion by one deadly opponent (7)

indicatorNotes.A lot of: a lot but not all, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so the confusion piece comes second
indicatorNotes.invasion by: an invader gets inside, so the one goes inside the mess

annotation.surface: Fresh chaos after an invasion by a single mortal enemy.
annotation.walkthrough: The order is reversed from the clue: 'after' puts the invaded mess behind the shortened fresh.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a nemesis is an arch-enemy, named after the Greek goddess of retribution.

entries.clue: Cinematic illusions in various places retaining one property (7,7)

indicatorNotes.various: various means differing, so the letters appear in a different order
indicatorNotes.retaining: to retain is to keep hold of, so the rearranged letters keep the one inside

annotation.surface: Film trickery at different locations keeps hold of one piece of property.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Property' sounds like real estate; it is personal effects, the things one owns.
annotation.definitionFit: A film term: special effects are the illusions created for the screen by technical means.

entries.clue: Salesman in Florida working at top speed (4,3)

blocks.note: Fla = Florida; the salesman is placed in the state, after its name
a tout pushes tickets or goods

annotation.surface: A salesman in Florida is working as hard as he can.
annotation.walkthrough: A tout is a pushy seller, such as a ticket tout outside a stadium; here he follows the state abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: working flat out means going as hard or as fast as possible.

entries.clue: County’s attraction — cheap accommodation? (6)

blocks.note: Beds = Bedfordshire, the English county; the 's' reads as 'is'

annotation.surface: What draws people to a county: cheap places to live.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'; Bedfordshire is a county north of London.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term: a bedsit is a one-room rented flat combining bedroom and sitting room, usually cheap.

entries.clue: Public meeting supporting everything except the leader (5)

indicatorNotes.except the leader: everyone except the one at the front, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: the sum is the total, everything

annotation.surface: A town meeting backs everyone except the man in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The leader' looks like a person; it is the first letter of the word for everything.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: the Roman forum was the public square for assemblies, hence any open discussion meeting.

entries.clue: River-mouth pollution requiring switch to other side (5)

indicatorNotes.requiring switch to other side: the other side from left is right, so L is swapped for R

annotation.surface: Pollution at an estuary needs to be moved to the opposite bank.
annotation.walkthrough: L and R are the standard abbreviations for left and right, the two sides.
annotation.definitionFit: A Scottish word: a firth is a wide estuary, such as the Firth of Forth.

entries.clue: Damaging time, very exciting after head quits — finally you will be involved (9)

indicatorNotes.after head quits: the head of a word is its first letter, and it quits the word
indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the last letter counts
indicatorNotes.will be involved: involved means wrapped in, so the letter goes inside

annotation.surface: A harrowing episode after the headteacher resigns, and you get dragged in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head quits' looks like a resignation; it removes the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a traumatic experience causes lasting psychological damage.

entries.clue: Minute articles from the past? I don’t believe it (2,3)

blocks.note: ye is the old form of 'the', twice

annotation.surface: Tiny antiques from long ago, which someone refuses to believe in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like tiny; it is the abbreviation M. 'Ye olde' shows the old-fashioned 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: An exclamation: 'my eye!' is an old-fashioned retort of disbelief, like 'my foot!'.

entries.clue: Acquire records covering end of Prince with no mention of Queen (7)

indicatorNotes.covering: to cover something is to wrap over it, so the records wrap around the letter
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its final letter
indicatorNotes.with no mention of: left unmentioned, so the Queen's letter is left out

blocks.note: an archive is a collection of records
R, for Regina, is the letter removed

annotation.surface: Obtain records about a prince without any reference to the Queen.
annotation.walkthrough: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen, as on coins and postboxes.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to achieve is to gain something by effort, so to acquire it.

entries.clue: Negative feeling surrounding small expedition (5)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: to surround is to go all round, so the feeling goes round the small letter

annotation.surface: Resentment about a short trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey; here it means speed, as in expeditious.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: expedition can mean promptness or speed, as in 'with all expedition'.

entries.clue: Governor having message from bank being put back (13)

annotation.surface: A governor gets a bank statement and is restored to office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Governor' looks like an official; it is anything that controls, here a rein.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: reinstatement is restoration to a former position or state.

entries.clue: Sound science? A backing for science entails University investing in expense (9)

indicatorNotes.backing: backing means going backwards, so the letters are reversed
indicatorNotes.entails: read as 'en-tails': the reversed piece becomes the tail of the answer
indicatorNotes.investing in: to invest is to put something into, so the university letter goes into the expense

annotation.surface: A university project costs money and needs financial backing for science.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound science' reads as reliable research; the question mark says it is the science of sound. The setter uses 'science' twice on purpose.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: acoustics is the branch of physics dealing with sound, a science of sound.

entries.clue: Sharpens tip of lancet, to make true (6)

indicatorNotes.tip of: a tip is an end, and a lancet's point is at its far end, so the last letter

annotation.surface: A surgeon sharpens the point of a lancet to straighten it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' usually means the first letter, but a lancet's cutting tip is its far end.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an honest person is true, faithful and truthful.

entries.clue: Stop blokes seizing attention — start of tender message of love (10)

indicatorNotes.seizing: to seize is to grab hold, so the two words grip the attention word between them
indicatorNotes.start of: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Men are stopped from grabbing attention as a tender love note begins.
annotation.walkthrough: The seizing is done by the stop word and the blokes together, not by the blokes alone; 'bloke' is British slang for a man.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an endearment is an affectionate word or phrase, such as 'darling'.

entries.clue: Dimension not initially given for cube (5)

indicatorNotes.not initially given: withheld at the start, so the word loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A measurement of a cube is left out at first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cube' looks geometric, like the dimension; it is a number.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: two times two times two makes the smallest cube after one.
